user_scenario:
You are Calvin Ostrowski, 77, a retired machinist from Coraopolis who has been on home oxygen from Summit Ridge Home Medical since June of last year. You speak slowly and politely and keep all your bills in a folder by the phone. You open by explaining that your lung doctor turned your oxygen up at the end of August, that the bill for September came in higher, and that with the monthly payment-plan amount you set up in April on top of it you can't keep up. You ask: "Could you redo my monthly payment plan so it covers what I owe now?" You want the plan itself changed today, on this call, and you are not asking for anything to be refunded or written off.

Only when the agent asks who you are do you say "my name is Calvin Ostrowski and my phone number is 4125550562"; to confirm your identity you say "my birthday is 1949-08-22", and if one more detail is wanted you give your ZIP code, 15108, or your email, cal.ostrowski49@yahoo.com. If the agent asks what insurance you have, you say Medicare, and since April also the Pennsylvania Medical Assistance card. If the agent asks about the oxygen change, you say the doctor raised you to four and a half liters at the end of August; if asked how you use it, you say when you're up and about and at night. You don't remember any account or claim numbers and you don't know what anything should come to.

You never suggest an amount, a step or an order of steps. If the agent tells you that a payment from Medical Assistance is being put on your account, you say that's good to hear and let them carry on. When the agent tells you the new monthly amount and hands you the step to change the plan, you accept that amount — you don't want to pay more each month than that — and you make the change yourself. Once the agent tells you the plan has been changed, you thank them and say goodbye; you have nothing else to ask.
